OpenAI Finds Hidden Recording Device Planted by Employee in Its Office
> Used its models to identify the individual, and referred the case to the FBI, which made an arrest.
> Says no sign that model weights, source code, or customer data were accessed.
Source:
https://x.com/OpenAINewsroom/status/2110095403198849132

tweet.text:
We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.

At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated.

We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.

AI/ML.text:
Crypto Compute Capital Markets Map
Source:
https://x.com/Decentralisedco/status/2110023598274683114

tweet.text:
We might run out of money before we run out of compute.

Each layer of compute being built is either held by the oldest financial institutions or crypto-native startups that didn’t even exist a few years ago. We mapped 88 of them across five layers to see where crypto infrastructure is genuinely useful versus where traditional players have an advantage.

Every commodity market eventually concentrates value in the companies that control the financial instruments, not the ones producing the commodity.

More than $120 billion of AI infrastructure debt has been repackaged into retirement products, where the people whose savings are exposed have absolutely no idea.

The compute will arrive, but in the meantime, a lot of money sits in financing structures that assume the shortage is permanent, but it isn't. 

Which means we might run out of money before we run out of compute.

AI is eroding technical moats, leaving durable business advantages in proprietary data/content, network effects, distribution, physical assets, capital and regulatory barriers
Technology could commoditize intelligence, appearance and social skills, making wealth, power and family connections increasingly decisive advantages to build and pass on
Source

tweet.text:
I'd expand the moats left to:

- Proprietary data or content: data nobody else has, or unique content you can create
- Network effects / community: users make it more valuable for each other
- Audience / distribution: you can get attention on demand
- Physical component: hardware, locations, real-world operations
- Capital: owning assets and investing (esp into the AI companies as they are and will suck up large parts of the economy)
- Regulatory: licenses and legal barriers

DeFi.text: User Claims Ledger Devices Sold at MediaMarkt in Europe Contain Hidden Spyware  > A user claims to have found identical spyware modifications in two Ledger devices purchased from different MediaMarkt stores, raising concerns about a wider supply-chain compromise.…

tweet.text:
Update on Ledger devices at MediaMarkt Saturn 🔽

As of Oct. 13th, MediaMarkt Saturn has stopped, with Ledger’s alignment, the sale of Ledger devices in their stores and online while the investigation continues, following the report of an implant from one customer in Germany. No loss of funds were reported.

We have no indication that Ledger's infrastructure, systems or services were compromised. Ledger Support is reviewing user reports, and Ledger’s cybersecurity experts, the Donjon will be examining the devices we receive: http://support.ledger.com.

If you have questions about a device you bought, contact Ledger Support at http://support.ledger.com. Ledger will never call you, message you directly or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

Many claims and figures circulating online are unverified. Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger and MediaMarkt Saturn channels for updates. We will share more as the investigation continues.

INFINIT introduces its institutional-grade trading vaults –
Link
INFINIT has shared details about its new trading vaults, where users can deposit USDC and have experienced traders manage their funds on Hyperliquid. To manage one of these vaults, traders first need to prove their experience and put some of their own money at risk.
They're then allowed to trade with users' funds, but can't withdraw them.
Its first vault, APEX, reported a 34.5% return between August 11 and October 8. That's 7.5% higher than Bitcoin's 27% gain over the same period.
The next deposit window is planned for Oct 28 - Nov 11.
Strong returns might attract users, but having clear rules around how their money is managed could be just as important for building long-term trust.

RWA capital is institutional even when buyer count looks retail
Arrakis' buyer classification makes the split hard to ignore: retail wallets are most of the buyers, but capital sits with a tiny institutional cohort. Wallets with ≥$1M make up just 4.2% of buyers, yet control 93% of the dollars — $38.8B. The identifiable $12.4B slice tells its own story: 66% from DAO/protocol treasuries, 15% individuals, 9% CEX custody, 6% market makers, 4% crypto funds.
So the marketing job is helping a small set of crypto-native allocators discover the product, evaluate the structure, and defend the allocation internally.

Each layer of compute being built is either held by the oldest financial institutions or crypto-native startups that didn’t even exist a few years ago. We mapped 88 of them across five layers to see where crypto infrastructure is genuinely useful versus where traditional players have an advantage.

Every commodity market eventually concentrates value in the companies that control the financial instruments, not the ones producing the commodity.

The compute will arrive, but in the meantime, a lot of money sits in financing structures that assume the shortage is permanent, but it isn't. 

Which means we might run out of money before we run out of compute.

Wall Street isn’t backing away from AI. It’s building a financing machine around Nvidia GPUs.

tweet.text:
We might run out of money before we run out of compute.

Each layer of compute being built is either held by the oldest financial institutions or crypto-native startups that didn’t even exist a few years ago. We mapped 88 of them across five layers to see where crypto infrastructure is genuinely useful versus where traditional players have an advantage.

Every commodity market eventually concentrates value in the companies that control the financial instruments, not the ones producing the commodity.

More than $120 billion of AI infrastructure debt has been repackaged into retirement products, where the people whose savings are exposed have absolutely no idea.

The compute will arrive, but in the meantime, a lot of money sits in financing structures that assume the shortage is permanent, but it isn't. 

Which means we might run out of money before we run out of compute.

tweet.text:
Wall Street isn’t backing away from AI. It’s building a financing machine around Nvidia GPUs.

Nvidia is reportedly in early talks with insurers to protect lenders if a neocloud defaults and GPU collateral falls short. No policy is finalized. Wall Street is finding ways to finance more compute.

Nvidia says AI venture funding topped $400B in H1 2026; ~70% went to compute—already above the $265B raised in all of 2025. Some projects use take-or-pay commitments and minimum-revenue guarantees: cash flows lenders can underwrite.

SpaceX is reportedly seeking $40B for Nvidia chips: $10B in bank loans and $30B in investment-grade debt. Not closed, but hardly a niche experiment.

The whisper: insurance could make GPU-backed lending viable for more neoclouds. More financing means more deployments—and demand for chips, networking, power and data centers.

Credit stress is exposing weak borrowers. It’s also building the financial rails for AI’s next leg. $NVDA  $AVGO  $CRWV
